title: Palantir Stock News (Oct 19, 2026): PLTR Falls 7.2% to $186.03
summary: Palantir (PLTR) fell 7.22% to $186.03 on Oct 16, 2026, as AI financing worries hit software stocks. What drove the drop and what to watch.
body_markdown:
## Why Palantir Stock Fell


No fetched source names a company-specific setback behind Friday's drop. As reported by[24/7 Wall St.](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/16/enterprise-software-stocks-fall-as-ai-financing-worries-spread-palantir-and-servicenow-drop-5-salesforce-slides-4/) on October 16, investors are questioning how AI infrastructure spending gets funded, and those doubts "feed directly into the pricing" of Palantir, ServiceNow and Salesforce. The outlet described the session as a rotation out of AI-linked stocks, with software taking the sharpest losses.


According to[FX Leaders](https://www.fxleaders.com/news/2026/10/16/pltr-stock-falls-below-190-as-ai-financing-risks-trigger-tech-sell-off/) , the pressure built earlier in the week after CoreWeave's bond yields climbed to a record, which revived concerns about debt-financed technology infrastructure, rising borrowing costs and stretched valuations. The outlet also noted that Palantir had set a record high shortly before, after Goldman Sachs revised its view on the stock, and that the reversal left the shares down about 10% for the week, a pattern consistent with profit-taking.


## PLTR Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- According to Palantir's[second-quarter 2026 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001321655/000132165526000039/a2026q2ex991pressrelease.htm) , revenue grew 93% year over year to $1.935 billion, and U.S. commercial revenue grew 149%.
- In the same release, Palantir raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to between $8.150 billion and $8.158 billion, and guided third-quarter revenue to between $2.160 billion and $2.164 billion.
- U.S. government revenue grew 90% year over year to $809 million, per the company's release.


### Risks


- 24/7 Wall St. argues that Palantir has little cushion when sentiment on AI-linked software turns, as Friday's drop showed.
- Per FX Leaders, rising borrowing costs and concerns about debt-financed AI infrastructure continue to weigh on AI-linked stocks.
- Volume ran 38.30% above average on the decline, showing heavy participation in the selling.


The third-quarter report is the next major event for the stock, and investors watching it can compare results against the company's own guidance; this guide on[how to read an earnings report](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/how-to-read-an-earnings-report/) explains what to look for. Palantir has not yet confirmed the date in a source fetched for this article.
